transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Alan Rivera (Peninsula Health - Head of Cloud Ops), Priya Nair (Security Lead), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Summary:
High-level discovery on Private/VPC deployment options for Redwood: customer is focused on on-prem/VPC model for PHI workflows, wants to understand connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), cross-account peering, region constraints, IP allowlists, KMS integration and SOC2/ISO artifacts. SE to run sizing/benchmark and propose Dedicated node config; AE to send architecture templates and security docs.

Topics:
- Connectivity options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect
- CIDR overlap, route tables, NAT/egress, private endpoints
- Cross-region considerations and region support for our private control plane
- Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, SOC2
- Next steps: documentation and benchmark scheduling

Action items (captured at top as well): see metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer. 
[00:08] Alan Rivera: Hi Maya, thanks. Alan here, I'll jump in on infra questions. Priya and Liam are on as well.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi, thanks.
[00:13] Diego Ramos: Hi all, Diego, SE. Quick note, I'll probably drill into network bits — routing, peering details — during the call.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Good to meet you both. We're considering Redwood for some of our PHI ingestion pipelines, so security and private connectivity are the big asks.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Perfect. High level first — could you outline current infra? What cloud, VPC layout, if you have Direct Connect, transit gateway, any on-prem?
[00:45] Alan Rivera: We're primarily on AWS us-east-1 and us-west-2, multiple accounts under a single org. We have a Transit Gateway for cross-account traffic and Direct Connect to our colo. Current VPCs use 10.0.0.0/8 split into /16s, some overlap historically with partner networks which we are cleaning up.
[01:06] Priya Nair: From security side, we need everything to stay in our VPC, no egress of raw data outside our control, and encryption keys must be customer-managed KMS. SOC2 and ISO are required for procurement.
[01:18] Diego Ramos: That's totally reasonable. Redwood supports a Private deployment where control plane can be customer-managed or we run a private control plane in your VPC — a couple of connectivity patterns there. Quick caveat: terminology sometimes mixes up — Redwood "Private" vs Redwood "Dedicated" — but for this call we mean our Private/VPC-hosted option.
[01:40] Alan Rivera: Right — can you walk through the connectivity options? We have constraints around CIDR overlap and can't punch holes through some partner VPCs.
[01:48] Diego Ramos: Sure. Option A is VPC Peering cross-account: simple, low latency, but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and you need peering set up per account pair. Option B is AWS PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints — that gives you a private ENI in your VPC that connects to our service in our account; it avoids peering and works across overlapping CIDRs but has per-ENI cost and some throughput limits. Option C is Transit Gateway attachment — scales better for many accounts but needs TGW routing and attachments. There's also Direct Connect/PrivateLink combinations for colo.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: Does PrivateLink support the large throughput we need? We plan to push batch inference loads and some streaming.
[02:35] Diego Ramos: PrivateLink can be fine for moderate throughput; we've seen customers on multi-ENI setups. For heavy sustained throughput, Transit Gateway or peered Dedicated VPCs with colocated GPU nodes is typically better. We'll need to size based on your token rates — we'll ask for sample workload.
[02:52] Priya Nair: About keys — our KMS policies are strict. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for model secrets and audit logs?
[03:00] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private can be configured to use your KMS for encryption at rest and to encrypt keys. For HSMs, we have partners and patterns (bring-your-own-hsm) though it's an advanced path; Diego can share design notes. We also provide audit logs and optional longer retention as an add-on.
[03:15] Alan Rivera: Great. Also curious about IP allowlists — we'll want to restrict inbound traffic to a small set of IPs for the control plane.
[03:22] Diego Ramos: We provide an IP allowlist template; for peering it's not needed but for PrivateLink/other endpoints you can restrict source security groups and SGs on the ENI. For hosted control plane endpoints, we publish static prefixes you can allowlist — we'll send the doc.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: Region support — if our PHI data is in us-east-1, can the compute be colocated there? We have latency requirements for sync pipelines.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Yes — we support deployments in major regions. For Private installs we typically provision nodes in the customer's region to meet residency & latency needs. There's some lead time — provisioning Dedicated GPU pools in region is part of sizing.
[03:58] Priya Nair: Any overlap issues? Our VPC ranges sometimes overlap with partner networks — you mentioned PrivateLink works with overlapping CIDRs; peering doesn't. Could you repeat tradeoffs?
[04:09] Diego Ramos: Sure — short: Peering = low latency, no NAT, but requires non-overlap; PrivateLink = works with overlap, easier cross-account, but you get ENIs and per-ENI resource limits; TGW is middle ground for many accounts, but adds complexity and cost. Also note route table entries and blackholing if misconfigured.
[04:30] Alan Rivera: Ok. For egress, do we see any public egress or does traffic stay within VPCs?
[04:36] Diego Ramos: If you choose a Private deployment with endpoints/peering, data can remain in your VPC and use peered routes — no public egress. If you use hosted API, then egress to Redwood's hosted control plane occurs over TLS, and you can use private link to avoid public internet.
[04:54] Priya Nair: Audit & logging — how do you expose logs? We need immutable audit trails for access to models and data ops.
[05:01] Maya Chen: We can ship audit logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Sentinel via a connector, or we can host them in our system with exported copies. Logs include token-level usage, model calls, and admin actions. Diego: any limitations?
[05:12] Diego Ramos: Just that for very high token-volume, log volume can be high — we recommend a sampling/ingestion plan or storage tiering. Also we support S3 export with server-side encryption using your KMS keys.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: Performance — for our workloads (avg prompt 1k tokens, ~300 qps at peak), what's the recommended sizing?
[05:36] Diego Ramos: Rough ballpark — depends on model size. If you're using a 13B model quantized to int8, and aiming for 300 qps with 1k tokens, you'd likely need multiple GPU nodes or a dedicated pool scaled horizontally. We should benchmark with a representative prompt set. I'll run a capacity estimate and share.
[05:56] Maya Chen: We'll also provide a template for the benchmark and a spreadsheet to capture latency/cost targets.
[06:02] Alan Rivera: On connectivity setup — who is responsible for peering requests and acceptance? We have strict change control windows.
[06:09] Maya Chen: Typically customer triggers peering from their side and we accept— for PrivateLink our infra team creates the service and you create the endpoint. We try to align with your maintenance windows. We'll document the steps.
[06:22] Priya Nair: Procurement: we need SOC2 + ISO docs before purchasing. Also a data processing agreement for PHI.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll share SOC2, ISO attestations, and our DPAs. For PHI specifically we have guidance and patterns but legal will want to review.
[06:38] Liam O'Connor: Any blockers on our side that would prevent a pilot?
[06:41] Diego Ramos: The main blockers are CIDR overlap and change-control timing. If you can provide current VPC CIDRs and a contact for peering ops, we can draft a plan.
[06:52] Alan Rivera: I'll extract CIDRs and peering owners and share.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Great. Recap: Maya to send architecture and IP allowlist doc + SOC2/ISO and DPA. Diego to run sizing/benchmark and propose node count. Customer to share CIDRs and peering contacts. We'll aim to schedule a benchmark week of 3/23. Any final questions?
[07:12] Priya Nair: One more quick: SSO/SAML— can we integrate with our IdP for RBAC?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Yes — we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, role-based access. We'll include mapping notes.
[07:24] Liam O'Connor: Ok thanks everyone.
[07:26] Alan Rivera: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:28] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and times for the benchmark.
